blurb.zh: 60 到 90 秒讲清现在的身份、做过的事和为什么来面这个岗位，最后把话头交还给面试官。
blurb.en: Cover where you are now, what you've built and why this role, in 60 to 90 seconds, then hand the floor back.

phrases.en: Sure, I'll give you a quick overview of my background.
phrases.zh: 好的，我简单介绍一下我的背景。

note.zh: quick overview 告诉对方你会控制时长，整段控制在 60–90 秒。
note.en: "Quick overview" signals you'll keep it short; aim for 60 to 90 seconds.

phrases.en: I'm currently a master's student in computer science at Northeastern, graduating in May.
phrases.zh: 我目前在东北大学读计算机硕士，五月毕业。

note.zh: 先说现在的身份和毕业时间，招聘方最关心你什么时候能入职。
note.en: Lead with where you are now and when you graduate; recruiters care about your start date.

phrases.en: Before that, I spent two years as a backend engineer at a fintech startup.
phrases.zh: 在那之前，我在一家金融科技创业公司做了两年后端工程师。

note.zh: 用 Before that 按时间往回讲，比照着简历逐条念自然。
note.en: "Before that" walks back in time; more natural than reading your resume line by line.

phrases.en: Most of my work there was on the payments API, which handled about two million requests a day.
phrases.zh: 我在那里主要负责支付 API，每天大约处理两百万次请求。

note.zh: 给一个具体数字，比 a lot of traffic 更有说服力。
note.en: One concrete number beats "a lot of traffic".

phrases.en: One project I'm especially proud of is a caching layer that cut our p99 latency in half.
phrases.zh: 我特别满意的一个项目是一个缓存层，把 p99 延迟降低了一半。

note.zh: 只挑一个项目讲结果，面试官多半会接着追问它。
note.en: Pick one project and its result; expect follow-up questions on it.

phrases.en: These days I'm mostly interested in distributed systems and developer tooling.
phrases.zh: 我现在主要对分布式系统和开发者工具感兴趣。

note.zh: 说兴趣方向时，挑和这个岗位相关的。
note.en: Name interests that connect to the role.

phrases.en: That's what drew me to this role.
phrases.zh: 这也是我被这个岗位吸引的原因。

note.zh: 把背景和岗位连起来，是收尾的好方式。
note.en: Tying your background to the job is a clean way to wrap up.

phrases.en: In a nutshell, I like building backend systems that are fast and easy to operate.
phrases.zh: 简单来说，我喜欢做又快又好运维的后端系统。

note.zh: In a nutshell 引出一句话总结，口语里很常见。
note.en: "In a nutshell" introduces a one-line summary; very common in speech.

phrases.en: I'm happy to go deeper into any of these.
phrases.zh: 哪一部分你想深入了解，我都可以展开讲。

note.zh: 把话头交还给面试官，避免一口气讲太久。
note.en: Hands the floor back so you don't ramble.

phrases.en: I go by Alex, by the way.
phrases.zh: 顺便说一下，叫我 Alex 就行。

note.zh: 有英文名或常用称呼时，这样说最自然。
note.en: The natural way to give the name you prefer.

dialogue.en: Hi, thanks for joining. Before we dive in, could you tell me a little about yourself?
dialogue.zh: 你好，谢谢参加。开始之前，能先简单介绍一下你自己吗？

dialogue.en: Sure. I'm a master's student in computer science, graduating in May. Before grad school, I worked for two years as a backend engineer at a fintech startup.
dialogue.zh: 好的。我是计算机硕士，五月毕业。读研之前，我在一家金融科技创业公司做了两年后端工程师。

dialogue.en: Nice. What did you work on there?
dialogue.zh: 不错。你在那里做什么？

dialogue.en: Mostly the payments API. One project I'm proud of is a caching layer that cut our p99 latency in half.
dialogue.zh: 主要是支付 API。我比较满意的一个项目是一个缓存层，把 p99 延迟降低了一半。

dialogue.en: Impressive. What are you looking for in your next role?
dialogue.zh: 很厉害。你下一份工作想找什么样的？

dialogue.en: I'd like to keep working on backend and distributed systems, ideally on a team where reliability really matters. That's what drew me to this role.
dialogue.zh: 我想继续做后端和分布式系统，最好在一个很看重可靠性的团队。这也是我被这个岗位吸引的原因。

dialogue.en: Great, that's helpful context.
dialogue.zh: 好的，这些背景很有帮助。

dialogue.en: Thanks. I'm happy to go deeper into any of that later.
dialogue.zh: 谢谢。之后哪部分想深入聊，我都可以展开。

cloze.en: Sure, I'll give you a quick ___ of my background.
cloze.zh: 好的，我简单介绍一下我的背景。

cloze.en: ___ that, I spent two years as a backend engineer.
cloze.zh: 在那之前，我做了两年后端工程师。

cloze.en: That's what ___ me to this role.
cloze.zh: 这就是我被这个岗位吸引的原因。

cloze.en: I'm happy to go ___ into any of these.
cloze.zh: 哪一部分我都可以深入讲。

parts: that cut our latency in half.
order.zh: 我特别满意的一个项目是一个把延迟降低一半的缓存层。
我现在主要对分布式系统和开发者工具感兴趣。

blurb.zh: 动手之前问清输入规模、边界和返回值，再用自己的话复述一遍题目。
blurb.en: Before coding, ask about input size, edge cases and return values, then restate the problem in your own words.

phrases.en: Before I start, can I ask a few clarifying questions?
phrases.zh: 开始之前，我可以问几个澄清问题吗？

note.zh: 几乎每道题都值得先问，面试官也在等你问。
note.en: Worth asking on almost every problem; interviewers expect it.

phrases.en: Just to make sure I understand, we need to return the indices, not the values?
phrases.zh: 我确认一下理解：要返回的是下标，不是值，对吗？

note.zh: 用自己的话复述题目，能及早发现误解。
note.en: Restating in your own words catches misunderstandings early.

phrases.en: What's the expected size of the input?
phrases.zh: 输入规模大概多大？

note.zh: 规模决定能接受的复杂度，比如十万量级通常排除 O(n²)。
note.en: Size tells you the acceptable complexity; a hundred thousand items usually rules out O(n²).

phrases.en: Can the array contain negative numbers or duplicates?
phrases.zh: 数组里会有负数或重复元素吗？

note.zh: 负数、重复、空输入是最常见的三类边界。
note.en: Negatives, duplicates and empty input are the classic edge cases.

phrases.en: Should I assume the input is always valid?
phrases.zh: 我可以假设输入总是合法的吗？

note.zh: 如果对方说不能，就说明你会怎么处理非法输入。
note.en: If not, say how you'd handle bad input.

phrases.en: What should the function return if there's no valid answer?
phrases.zh: 如果没有合法答案，函数应该返回什么？

note.zh: 返回 -1、空列表还是抛异常，先问清楚。
note.en: Minus one, an empty list or an exception: settle it up front.

phrases.en: Is the input sorted, or am I allowed to sort it?
phrases.zh: 输入是有序的吗？我可以先排序吗？

note.zh: 能不能改动或排序输入，常常决定解法。
note.en: Whether you can reorder the input often decides the approach.

phrases.en: Are we optimizing for time or memory here?
phrases.zh: 这题更看重时间还是空间？

note.zh: 让面试官说出偏好，后面讲取舍时有依据。
note.en: Getting their preference lets you justify trade-offs later.

phrases.en: Let me write down a quick example to check my understanding.
phrases.zh: 我写一个小例子确认一下理解。

note.zh: 边写边说，面试官能及时纠正你。
note.en: Say it as you write so they can correct you early.

phrases.en: So the input is a list of intervals, and the output is the merged list. Does that sound right?
phrases.zh: 所以输入是一组区间，输出是合并后的列表，对吗？

note.zh: Does that sound right? 比 Am I right? 更柔和自然。
note.en: "Does that sound right?" sounds softer than "Am I right?".

dialogue.en: Given an array of integers and a target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to the target.
dialogue.zh: 给定一个整数数组和一个目标值，返回和为目标值的两个数的下标。

dialogue.en: Okay. Before I start, can I ask a few clarifying questions?
dialogue.zh: 好的。开始之前，我可以问几个澄清问题吗？

dialogue.en: Of course.
dialogue.zh: 当然。

dialogue.en: Can the array contain duplicates or negative numbers?
dialogue.zh: 数组里会有重复或负数吗？

dialogue.en: Both are possible.
dialogue.zh: 都有可能。

dialogue.en: And is there always exactly one valid pair, or should I handle the case where there's none?
dialogue.zh: 是一定恰好有一对答案，还是我也要处理没有答案的情况？

dialogue.en: You can assume there's exactly one answer.
dialogue.zh: 你可以假设恰好有一个答案。

dialogue.en: Got it. And roughly how large can the array be?
dialogue.zh: 明白。数组最大大概多大？

dialogue.en: Up to a hundred thousand elements.
dialogue.zh: 最多十万个元素。

dialogue.en: Okay, so checking every pair is probably too slow. Let me write down a quick example to check my understanding.
dialogue.zh: 好，那检查每一对可能太慢了。我写个小例子确认一下理解。

cloze.en: Before I start, can I ask a few ___ questions?
cloze.zh: 开始之前，我可以问几个澄清问题吗？

cloze.en: Just to make sure I ___, we need to return the indices?
cloze.zh: 我确认一下理解：要返回的是下标吗？

cloze.en: What should the function return if there's no ___ answer?
cloze.zh: 如果没有合法答案，函数应该返回什么？

cloze.en: Are we optimizing for time or ___ here?
cloze.zh: 这题更看重时间还是空间？

order.zh: 所以输入是一组区间，输出是合并后的列表。
我可以假设输入总是合法的吗？

blurb.zh: 先讲思路再写代码，写到关键行时说清在做什么，卡住或改主意时也说出来。
blurb.en: Explain the plan before coding, narrate the key lines, and say it out loud when you pause or change your mind.

phrases.en: Let me talk through my approach before I write any code.
phrases.zh: 写代码之前，我先讲一下思路。

note.zh: 先讲再写，面试官能在你走偏前提醒你。
note.en: Explaining first lets them steer you before you go too far.

phrases.en: My first thought is a brute-force solution: check every pair.
phrases.zh: 我第一个想法是暴力解：检查每一对。

note.zh: 先说暴力解再优化，是完全正常的节奏。
note.en: Starting with brute force and improving it is a normal rhythm.

phrases.en: I think we can do better with a hash map.
phrases.zh: 我觉得用哈希表能做得更好。

note.zh: do better 是说“有更优解”的日常说法。
note.en: "Do better" is the everyday way to say "optimize".

phrases.en: I'm going to start with a helper function that parses the input.
phrases.zh: 我先写一个解析输入的辅助函数。

note.zh: 用 I'm going to 预告下一步，让对方跟得上。
note.en: "I'm going to" previews your next step so they can follow.

phrases.en: Here I'm looping through the array and storing each value's index.
phrases.zh: 这里我遍历数组，把每个值的下标存起来。

note.zh: 写到关键行时说一句“这里在做什么”。
note.en: Narrate what the key lines do as you write them.

phrases.en: I'll use a deque here, since we need to pop from both ends.
phrases.zh: 这里我用双端队列，因为两端都要弹出。

note.zh: 选数据结构时顺便用 since 或 because 说原因。
note.en: Give a reason with "since" or "because" when you pick a structure.

phrases.en: Let me pause for a second and think about the edge cases.
phrases.zh: 我停一下，想想边界情况。

note.zh: 需要思考时说出来，比长时间沉默好。
note.en: Saying you need a moment beats a long silence.

phrases.en: I'll come back to this part. For now, let's assume it works.
phrases.zh: 这部分我稍后回来处理，现在先假设它是对的。

note.zh: 先跳过细节保持进度，但记得回来补上。
note.en: Skip a detail to keep moving, and make sure you come back.

phrases.en: Actually, wait, I don't think this handles an empty list.
phrases.zh: 等一下，我觉得这里没处理空列表。

note.zh: 自己发现错误时直接说出来，这是加分项。
note.en: Catching your own bug out loud is a plus.

phrases.en: I'm calling this variable left, since it marks the start of the window.
phrases.zh: 我把这个变量叫 left，因为它标记窗口的起点。

note.zh: 解释命名，顺便也说明了你的思路。
note.en: Explaining a name explains your logic too.

dialogue.en: Okay, go ahead whenever you're ready.
dialogue.zh: 好，准备好了就开始吧。

dialogue.en: Sure. Let me talk through my approach before I write any code. My first thought is to check every pair, but that's quadratic.
dialogue.zh: 好的。写代码前我先讲讲思路。第一个想法是检查每一对，但那是平方级的。

dialogue.en: Right. Can you improve on that?
dialogue.zh: 对。能改进吗？

dialogue.en: I think we can do better with a hash map. As I go through the array, I'll store each value's index, and for each number I'll check whether its complement is already in the map.
dialogue.zh: 我觉得用哈希表能更好。遍历数组时，我把每个值的下标存起来，对每个数检查它的补数是否已经在表里。

dialogue.en: Sounds good. Go ahead and code it up.
dialogue.zh: 听起来不错，写出来吧。

dialogue.en: Okay, I'm going to start with the loop. Here I'm computing the complement, which is the target minus the current number.
dialogue.zh: 好，我先写循环。这里在算补数，也就是目标值减去当前数。

dialogue.en: Actually, wait, I should check the map before inserting the current number. Otherwise I might pair a number with itself.
dialogue.zh: 等一下，我应该先查表再插入当前数，不然可能会把一个数和它自己配对。

dialogue.en: Good catch.
dialogue.zh: 发现得好。

cloze.en: Let me talk ___ my approach before I write any code.
cloze.zh: 写代码之前，我先讲一下思路。

cloze.en: I think we can do ___ with a hash map.
cloze.zh: 我觉得用哈希表能做得更好。

cloze.en: Let me ___ for a second and think about the edge cases.
cloze.zh: 我停一下，想想边界情况。

cloze.en: I'll use a deque here, ___ we need to pop from both ends.
cloze.zh: 这里我用双端队列，因为两端都要弹出。

order.zh: 我第一个想法是暴力解：检查每一对。

parts: I'll come back to this part.
order.zh: 这部分我稍后回来处理，现在先假设它是对的。

blurb.zh: 把大 O 念出来：时间和空间一起说，区分平均和最坏，并说明拿什么换什么。
blurb.en: Say big O out loud: time and space together, average versus worst case, and what you trade for what.

phrases.en: This runs in O of n time, since we only go through the array once.
phrases.zh: 这是 O(n) 时间，因为只遍历一次数组。

note.zh: O(n) 读作 O of n，也可以说 linear time。
note.en: Written O(n), said "O of n", or simply "linear time".

phrases.en: The space complexity is O of n as well, because of the hash map.
phrases.zh: 空间复杂度也是 O(n)，因为用了哈希表。

note.zh: 说完时间马上补空间，别等面试官问。
note.en: Give space right after time; don't wait to be asked.

phrases.en: Sorting dominates, so overall it's O of n log n.
phrases.zh: 排序是主要开销，所以总体是 O(n log n)。

note.zh: dominates 用来说哪一步决定了总复杂度。
note.en: "Dominates" names the step that sets the overall cost.

phrases.en: In the worst case, every element ends up in the same bucket.
phrases.zh: 最坏情况下，所有元素都落在同一个桶里。

note.zh: 说最坏情况时，讲清楚具体会发生什么。
note.en: Say what actually happens in the worst case.

phrases.en: On average it's constant time, but the worst case is linear.
phrases.zh: 平均是常数时间，但最坏是线性的。

note.zh: 哈希表、快排这类要区分平均和最坏。
note.en: For hash maps and quicksort, separate the average from the worst case.

phrases.en: Each element is pushed and popped at most once, so it's amortized O of 1.
phrases.zh: 每个元素最多入栈、出栈各一次，所以均摊是 O(1)。

note.zh: amortized（均摊）在单调栈、动态数组里常用。
note.en: "Amortized" comes up with monotonic stacks and dynamic arrays.

phrases.en: We could trade some memory for speed by caching the results.
phrases.zh: 我们可以缓存结果，拿空间换时间。

note.zh: trade X for Y 是“用 X 换 Y”，讲取舍的万能句式。
note.en: "Trade X for Y" is the go-to pattern for trade-offs.

phrases.en: If we can't use extra space, we could sort in place instead, at the cost of O of n log n time.
phrases.zh: 如果不能用额外空间，可以改成原地排序，代价是 O(n log n) 时间。

note.zh: 用 at the cost of 说清代价。
note.en: "At the cost of" states the price.

phrases.en: Here n is the number of nodes and m is the number of edges.
phrases.zh: 这里 n 是节点数，m 是边数。

note.zh: 有多个变量时，先说清每个字母代表什么。
note.en: With several variables, define each letter first.

phrases.en: The recursion goes at most log n levels deep, so the stack uses O of log n space.
phrases.zh: 递归最多 log n 层，所以栈空间是 O(log n)。

note.zh: 递归的栈空间容易被忘记，主动提到。
note.en: Recursion stack space is easy to forget; bring it up yourself.

dialogue.en: What's the time complexity of your solution?
dialogue.zh: 你的解法时间复杂度是多少？

dialogue.en: It's O of n log n. Sorting dominates; the scan afterwards is linear.
dialogue.zh: O(n log n)。排序是主要开销，之后的扫描是线性的。

dialogue.en: And space?
dialogue.zh: 空间呢？

dialogue.en: O of n for the sorted copy. If we're allowed to modify the input, we could sort in place and bring it down to O of log n for the recursion stack.
dialogue.zh: 排序后的副本要 O(n)。如果允许修改输入，可以原地排序，降到递归栈的 O(log n)。

dialogue.en: Could you do it faster than n log n?
dialogue.zh: 能比 n log n 更快吗？

dialogue.en: We could use a hash set to get O of n time on average, but we'd trade that for O of n extra space.
dialogue.zh: 可以用哈希集合，平均 O(n) 时间，但要多用 O(n) 空间。

dialogue.en: Which one would you pick?
dialogue.zh: 你会选哪个？

dialogue.en: It depends on the input size and the memory limit. For a hundred thousand elements, I'd go with the hash set, since the extra memory is small.
dialogue.zh: 取决于输入规模和内存限制。十万个元素的话我会用哈希集合，因为多出来的内存很小。

cloze.en: Sorting ___, so overall it's O of n log n.
cloze.zh: 排序是主要开销，所以总体是 O(n log n)。

cloze.en: On ___ it's constant time, but the worst case is linear.
cloze.zh: 平均是常数时间，但最坏是线性的。

cloze.en: We could ___ some memory for speed by caching the results.
cloze.zh: 我们可以缓存结果，拿空间换时间。

cloze.en: We could sort in place, at the ___ of more time.
cloze.zh: 可以原地排序，代价是更多时间。

order.zh: 每个元素最多入栈、出栈各一次，所以均摊是 O(1)。
这里 n 是节点数，m 是边数。

blurb.zh: 说清卡在哪一点、试过什么，再要一个方向；拿到提示后马上说出怎么用。
blurb.en: Say exactly where you're stuck and what you tried, ask for a direction, then show how you'll use the hint.

phrases.en: I'm a bit stuck on how to handle the duplicates.
phrases.zh: 我在怎么处理重复元素上有点卡住了。

note.zh: 说清卡在哪一点，比只说 I'm stuck 有用得多。
note.en: Say exactly where you're stuck, not just "I'm stuck".

phrases.en: Here's what I've tried so far.
phrases.zh: 这是我目前试过的思路。

note.zh: 先说试过什么，面试官才知道该给什么提示。
note.en: Showing what you tried tells them which hint to give.

phrases.en: Could you give me a small hint?
phrases.zh: 可以给我一点小提示吗？

note.zh: small hint 表示你只要方向，不要答案。
note.en: "Small hint" asks for a nudge, not the answer.

phrases.en: Am I on the right track with the two-pointer idea?
phrases.zh: 我用双指针的思路，方向对吗？

note.zh: 确认方向是很自然的问法，不算直接要答案。
note.en: Checking your direction is natural and isn't asking for the answer.

phrases.en: I'm torn between a heap and sorting. Which direction would you like me to explore?
phrases.zh: 我在堆和排序之间犹豫，你希望我往哪个方向走？

note.zh: 给出两个选项让对方选，说明你是有思路的。
note.en: Offering two options shows you have ideas.

phrases.en: Let me think out loud for a minute.
phrases.zh: 我先出声想一分钟。

note.zh: 卡住时继续说话，面试官能看到你的推理。
note.en: Keep talking when stuck so they can see your reasoning.

phrases.en: Is there a property of the input I might be missing?
phrases.zh: 输入有没有什么性质是我可能忽略的？

note.zh: 问输入的性质，是一种体面的求提示方式。
note.en: Asking about the input is a graceful way to fish for a hint.

phrases.en: Okay, that helps a lot. So if the array is sorted, I can use binary search.
phrases.zh: 好，这很有帮助。那如果数组有序，我就可以用二分查找。

note.zh: 拿到提示后马上说出你打算怎么用它。
note.en: Show right away how you'll use the hint.

phrases.en: That makes sense. Let me see how that changes my approach.
phrases.zh: 有道理，我看看这会怎么改变我的思路。

note.zh: 接住提示，然后继续往前推进。
note.en: Acknowledge the hint, then keep moving.

phrases.en: I don't want to spend too long here. Would it be okay if I go with the simpler version first?
phrases.zh: 我不想在这里耽误太久，我先写简单版本可以吗？

note.zh: 时间紧时主动提出降级方案，显得有判断力。
note.en: Offering a simpler version when time is short shows judgment.

dialogue.en: I'm a bit stuck on how to avoid counting the same window twice.
dialogue.zh: 我在怎么避免同一个窗口被算两次上有点卡住了。

dialogue.en: Okay. What have you tried?
dialogue.zh: 好，你试过什么？

dialogue.en: I tried storing every window in a set, but that uses way too much memory. Am I on the right track with a sliding window at all?
dialogue.zh: 我试过把每个窗口存进集合，但那样内存占用太大了。滑动窗口这个方向本身对吗？

dialogue.en: Yes, a sliding window is the right idea. Think about what changes when the window moves by one.
dialogue.zh: 对，滑动窗口是对的。想想窗口移动一格时会变化什么。

dialogue.en: Oh, I see. Only one element leaves and one enters, so I can update the count instead of recomputing it.
dialogue.zh: 哦，我明白了。只有一个元素出去、一个元素进来，所以我可以更新计数，而不用重新计算。

dialogue.en: Exactly.
dialogue.zh: 没错。

dialogue.en: That makes sense. Let me see how that changes my loop.
dialogue.zh: 有道理，我看看这对循环有什么影响。

cloze.en: Could you give me a small ___?
cloze.zh: 可以给我一点小提示吗？

cloze.en: Am I on the right ___ with the two-pointer idea?
cloze.zh: 我用双指针的思路，方向对吗？

cloze.en: Here's what I've ___ so far.
cloze.zh: 这是我目前试过的思路。

cloze.en: Is there a property of the input I might be ___?
cloze.zh: 输入有没有什么性质是我可能忽略的？

parts: would you like me to explore?
order.zh: 我在堆和排序之间犹豫，你希望我往哪个方向走？
有道理，我看看这会怎么改变我的思路。

blurb.zh: 写完先用小例子走一遍，念出变量的值，再列边界情况，发现问题当场修。
blurb.en: Trace a small example and read out the variables, list the edge cases, and fix what you find on the spot.

phrases.en: Let me walk through a quick example to make sure this works.
phrases.zh: 我用一个小例子走一遍，确认代码没问题。

note.zh: 写完先说这句，别等面试官要求。
note.en: Say this as soon as you finish; don't wait to be asked.

phrases.en: I'll trace through it with the input one, three, two.
phrases.zh: 我用输入 1、3、2 跟踪一遍。

note.zh: 数字一个一个念，别连起来像 one thirty-two。
note.en: Read the numbers one by one so they don't run together.

phrases.en: At this point, left is zero and right is two.
phrases.zh: 这时 left 是 0，right 是 2。

note.zh: 跟踪时说出关键变量的值。
note.en: Say the key variables' values as you trace.

phrases.en: So after the first iteration, the map contains three.
phrases.zh: 所以第一轮之后，表里有 3。

note.zh: iteration 指循环的一轮。
note.en: An iteration is one pass of the loop.

phrases.en: That matches the expected output.
phrases.zh: 和期望输出一致。

note.zh: 跟踪完一定要和预期结果对一下。
note.en: Always compare the trace with the expected output.

phrases.en: Now let me try some edge cases: an empty array, a single element, and all duplicates.
phrases.zh: 现在试几个边界情况：空数组、单个元素、全部重复。

note.zh: 先一口气列出几个边界，再逐个检查。
note.en: List a few edge cases, then check them one by one.

phrases.en: Hmm, this would fail if the input is empty, so I'll add a check at the top.
phrases.zh: 嗯，输入为空时会出错，我在开头加个判断。

note.zh: 发现问题就当场修，并说出改了什么。
note.en: Fix it on the spot and say what you changed.

phrases.en: There's an off-by-one error here. The loop should stop at n minus one.
phrases.zh: 这里有个差一错误，循环应该在 n-1 停。

note.zh: off-by-one 是“差一错误”的标准说法。
note.en: "Off-by-one" is the standard term.

phrases.en: If I had more time, I'd write unit tests for the overflow case.
phrases.zh: 如果时间更多，我会给溢出的情况写单元测试。

note.zh: 来不及做的测试，用 If I had more time 带过。
note.en: Mention the tests you'd add with "If I had more time".

phrases.en: I'm fairly confident this is correct now.
phrases.zh: 我现在比较有把握这是对的。

note.zh: fairly confident 显得稳，又不过度自信。
note.en: "Fairly confident" sounds steady without overclaiming.

dialogue.en: Looks like you're done. How would you check that it works?
dialogue.zh: 看起来写完了。你会怎么确认它是对的？

dialogue.en: Let me walk through a quick example. I'll use the input two, seven, eleven, fifteen, with a target of nine.
dialogue.zh: 我用一个小例子走一遍：输入 2、7、11、15，目标 9。

dialogue.en: On the first iteration, we see two. Its complement is seven, which isn't in the map yet, so we store two.
dialogue.zh: 第一轮看到 2，它的补数是 7，还不在表里，所以把 2 存进去。

dialogue.en: On the second iteration, we see seven, and its complement two is in the map, so we return zero and one. That matches the expected output.
dialogue.zh: 第二轮看到 7，补数 2 在表里，所以返回 0 和 1。和期望输出一致。

dialogue.en: What about edge cases?
dialogue.zh: 那边界情况呢？

dialogue.en: If the array has fewer than two elements, the loop never finds a pair. The problem says there's always an answer, but I'd still raise an error there instead of returning nothing.
dialogue.zh: 如果数组少于两个元素，循环永远找不到一对。题目说一定有答案，但我还是会在这里抛错误，而不是什么都不返回。

dialogue.en: Sounds reasonable.
dialogue.zh: 合理。

dialogue.en: And if the same number appears twice, like three and three with a target of six, it still works, because we check the map before inserting.
dialogue.zh: 如果同一个数出现两次，比如 3 和 3、目标 6，也没问题，因为我们是先查表再插入。

cloze.en: Let me ___ through a quick example to make sure this works.
cloze.zh: 我用一个小例子走一遍，确认代码没问题。

cloze.en: That ___ the expected output.
cloze.zh: 和期望输出一致。

cloze.en: There's an off-by-___ error here.
cloze.zh: 这里有个差一错误。

cloze.en: If I had more time, I'd write unit ___ for the overflow case.
cloze.zh: 如果时间更多，我会给溢出的情况写单元测试。

order.zh: 现在试几个边界情况：空数组和单个元素。
我现在比较有把握这是对的。

blurb.zh: 对方指出问题时先承认再改；你确信自己是对的时，礼貌地坚持并给出理由。
blurb.en: When they spot a problem, acknowledge it and fix it; when you're sure you're right, hold your ground politely and explain.

phrases.en: That's a good point. I hadn't considered that case.
phrases.zh: 说得好，我没考虑到这种情况。

note.zh: 先承认再改，比急着辩解好。
note.en: Acknowledge first, then fix; better than getting defensive.

phrases.en: You're right, that would break if the list is empty.
phrases.zh: 你说得对，列表为空时会出问题。

note.zh: 说出具体在哪里出问题，表明你真的理解了。
note.en: Naming where it breaks shows you actually understood.

phrases.en: Let me double-check that.
phrases.zh: 我再确认一下。

note.zh: 被质疑但不确定时，先查再回答。
note.en: When challenged and unsure, check before answering.

phrases.en: I think it still works here, and here's why.
phrases.zh: 我认为这里还是对的，原因是这样的。

note.zh: 确信自己是对的时，礼貌地坚持并给出理由。
note.en: If you're sure you're right, hold your ground politely and explain.

phrases.en: Could you tell me a bit more about what you're thinking?
phrases.zh: 能多说一点你的想法吗？

note.zh: 没听懂提示就请对方展开，别假装听懂。
note.en: If you didn't get the hint, ask; don't pretend.

phrases.en: So you're suggesting we process it from the right instead?
phrases.zh: 所以你是建议我们改成从右往左处理？

note.zh: 先复述提示，确认理解对了再动手。
note.en: Restate the hint before acting on it.

phrases.en: That's a fair concern. One way to address it would be to add a lock.
phrases.zh: 这个顾虑很合理，一种解决办法是加锁。

note.zh: 先用 fair concern 认可，再给方案。
note.en: "Fair concern" validates the point; then offer a fix.

phrases.en: I went with this approach because it's simpler, but I'm happy to optimize it.
phrases.zh: 我选这个方法是因为它更简单，不过我很乐意再优化。

note.zh: 解释当初的选择，同时表示愿意调整。
note.en: Explain your choice and show you're open to changing it.

phrases.en: Good catch. Let me fix that.
phrases.zh: 发现得好，我改一下。

note.zh: 被指出 bug 时最简洁的回应。
note.en: The shortest good response when someone spots a bug.

phrases.en: Thanks, that hint really helps.
phrases.zh: 谢谢，这个提示很有用。

note.zh: 简单道谢就好，不用反复道歉。
note.en: A quick thanks is enough; no need to keep apologizing.

dialogue.en: What happens if two intervals share an endpoint, like one to three and three to five?
dialogue.zh: 如果两个区间共用一个端点，比如 1 到 3 和 3 到 5，会怎样？

dialogue.en: Good question. Right now I'm using a strict less-than, so they'd stay separate.
dialogue.zh: 好问题。我现在用的是严格小于，所以它们会保持分开。

dialogue.en: Is that what we want?
dialogue.zh: 这是我们想要的吗？

dialogue.en: You're right, they should be merged, since they touch. I'll change it to less-than-or-equal.
dialogue.zh: 你说得对，它们相接，应该合并。我改成小于等于。

dialogue.en: Also, why sort by start time instead of end time?
dialogue.zh: 另外，为什么按开始时间排序，而不是结束时间？

dialogue.en: I think start time is the right choice here, and here's why: once the intervals are sorted by start, anything that overlaps the current merged interval has to come right after it.
dialogue.zh: 我认为这里按开始时间是对的，原因是：按开始时间排好之后，和当前合并区间重叠的区间一定紧跟在它后面。

dialogue.en: Okay, that makes sense.
dialogue.zh: 好，有道理。

dialogue.en: Thanks for pointing out the endpoint case. That would have been a nasty bug.
dialogue.zh: 谢谢你指出端点的情况，那会是个很麻烦的 bug。

cloze.en: That's a good ___. I hadn't considered that case.
cloze.zh: 说得好，我没考虑到这种情况。

cloze.en: Let me double-___ that.
cloze.zh: 我再确认一下。

cloze.en: That's a ___ concern. One way to address it would be to add a lock.
cloze.zh: 这个顾虑很合理，一种解决办法是加锁。

cloze.en: Good ___. Let me fix that.
cloze.zh: 发现得好，我改一下。

order.zh: 我认为这里还是对的，原因是这样的。
所以你是建议我们改成从右往左处理？

blurb.zh: 用固定的过渡句把背景、任务、行动、结果串起来，行动部分讲清你本人做了什么。
blurb.en: Link Situation, Task, Action and Result with set transitions, and make the Action about what you did.

phrases.en: Sure, a situation that comes to mind is from my internship last summer.
phrases.zh: 好的，我想到的一个例子是去年夏天实习时的事。

note.zh: comes to mind 是开始讲故事的自然开头。
note.en: "Comes to mind" is a natural way to start a story.

phrases.en: For some context, our team owned the checkout service.
phrases.zh: 先交代一下背景，我们团队负责结账服务。

note.zh: For some context 引出背景（S），一两句就够。
note.en: "For some context" opens the Situation; one or two sentences is enough.

phrases.en: My job was to cut the page load time before the holiday sale.
phrases.zh: 我的任务是在节日促销前缩短页面加载时间。

note.zh: My job was 或 I was responsible for 引出任务（T）。
note.en: "My job was" or "I was responsible for" introduces the Task.

phrases.en: The challenge was that we only had three weeks.
phrases.zh: 难点在于我们只有三周时间。

note.zh: 点出难点，故事才有张力。
note.en: Naming the challenge gives the story tension.

phrases.en: So the first thing I did was profile the slowest requests.
phrases.zh: 所以我做的第一件事是分析最慢的请求。

note.zh: 行动（A）部分多说 I、少说 we，讲清你本人做了什么。
note.en: In the Action part say "I", not "we": show what you did.

phrases.en: Then I worked with the frontend team to lazy-load the images.
phrases.zh: 然后我和前端团队合作，把图片改成懒加载。

note.zh: 用 Then、After that 把行动按顺序串起来。
note.en: "Then" and "After that" chain your actions in order.

phrases.en: As a result, the load time dropped by forty percent.
phrases.zh: 结果加载时间降低了 40%。

note.zh: As a result 引出结果（R），尽量给数字。
note.en: "As a result" opens the Result; give a number if you can.

phrases.en: Looking back, I'd involve the other team earlier.
phrases.zh: 回头看，我会更早让另一个团队参与。

note.zh: 最后补一句反思，显得成熟。
note.en: A short reflection at the end shows maturity.

phrases.en: What I learned from that is to ask for help sooner.
phrases.zh: 我从中学到的是要更早寻求帮助。

note.zh: What I learned 是讲收获的标准句式。
note.en: "What I learned" is the standard way to share the takeaway.

phrases.en: Does that answer your question, or would you like more detail on any part?
phrases.zh: 这样回答了你的问题吗？还是哪部分想听更多细节？

note.zh: 讲完确认一下，让面试官决定要不要深挖。
note.en: Check in at the end and let them choose what to dig into.

dialogue.en: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate.
dialogue.zh: 讲一次你和队友意见不合的经历。

dialogue.en: Sure. A situation that comes to mind is from my last internship. For some context, we were building a new notification service.
dialogue.zh: 好的。我想到的是上一次实习的事。先交代一下背景，我们当时在做一个新的通知服务。

dialogue.en: My teammate wanted to send every notification synchronously, and I was worried about latency under load.
dialogue.zh: 我的队友想让所有通知同步发送，而我担心高负载下的延迟。

dialogue.en: How did you handle it?
dialogue.zh: 你是怎么处理的？

dialogue.en: The first thing I did was write a quick load test, so we could compare both designs with real numbers. Then I set up a short meeting to go over the results together.
dialogue.zh: 我做的第一件事是写一个简单的压测，用真实数据比较两种设计。然后我约了一个短会，一起看结果。

dialogue.en: And what happened?
dialogue.zh: 结果如何？

dialogue.en: As a result, we went with a queue, and our p99 latency stayed under two hundred milliseconds at peak. My teammate actually ended up owning the queue work.
dialogue.zh: 结果我们选择了队列，高峰时 p99 延迟保持在 200 毫秒以内。我的队友后来还主动负责了队列这部分。

dialogue.en: Looking back, what I learned is that data settles a disagreement faster than opinions do.
dialogue.zh: 回头看，我学到的是：用数据解决分歧比用观点快。

cloze.en: Sure, a situation that comes to ___ is from my internship.
cloze.zh: 好的，我想到的一个例子是实习时的事。

cloze.en: For some ___, our team owned the checkout service.
cloze.zh: 先交代一下背景，我们团队负责结账服务。

cloze.en: As a ___, the load time dropped by forty percent.
cloze.zh: 结果加载时间降低了 40%。

cloze.en: Looking ___, I'd involve the other team earlier.
cloze.zh: 回头看，我会更早让另一个团队参与。

order.zh: 所以我做的第一件事是分析最慢的请求。
我从中学到的是要更早寻求帮助。

title.zh: 系统设计：推进讨论、讲取舍

blurb.zh: 先定需求和规模，再给高层设计，主动讲取舍和瓶颈，并把下一步的选择交给面试官。
blurb.en: Pin down requirements and scale, sketch the high-level design, raise trade-offs and bottlenecks, and let them pick the next deep dive.

phrases.en: Before jumping into the design, I'd like to nail down the requirements.
phrases.zh: 在开始设计之前，我想先把需求定下来。

note.zh: nail down 是“敲定”的口语说法。
note.en: "Nail down" is casual for "settle".

phrases.en: Should we focus on reads or writes? I'd guess this is read-heavy.
phrases.zh: 我们重点看读还是写？我猜这是读多写少。

note.zh: 主动给出你的猜测，让面试官确认。
note.en: Offer your guess and let them confirm it.

phrases.en: Let me do a quick back-of-the-envelope estimate.
phrases.zh: 我先粗略估算一下。

note.zh: back-of-the-envelope 指粗略估算。
note.en: "Back-of-the-envelope" means a rough estimate.

phrases.en: Here's a high-level design, and then we can dive into whichever part you'd like.
phrases.zh: 先给一个高层设计，然后你想深入哪部分都可以。

note.zh: 先画全貌，再让面试官选深挖点。
note.en: Sketch the big picture, then let them pick a deep dive.

phrases.en: The main trade-off here is consistency versus availability.
phrases.zh: 这里的主要取舍是一致性和可用性。

note.zh: trade-off 是系统设计里出现最多的词之一。
note.en: "Trade-off" is one of the most used words in a design round.

phrases.en: We could use a relational database, but given the write volume, I'd lean toward a key-value store.
phrases.zh: 可以用关系型数据库，但考虑到写入量，我更倾向于键值存储。

note.zh: I'd lean toward 表达倾向，但不武断。
note.en: "I'd lean toward" states a preference without sounding absolute.

phrases.en: The downside is that we lose strong consistency, which I think is acceptable for a news feed.
phrases.zh: 缺点是失去强一致性，我认为对信息流来说可以接受。

note.zh: 说出缺点，并说明为什么在这里可以接受。
note.en: State the downside and why it's acceptable here.

phrases.en: One bottleneck I see is the database during peak hours.
phrases.zh: 我看到的一个瓶颈是高峰期的数据库。

note.zh: 主动找瓶颈，是高分表现。
note.en: Spotting bottlenecks yourself scores well.

phrases.en: To keep an eye on the time, should I move on to the API, or go deeper on storage?
phrases.zh: 考虑到时间，我是先讲 API，还是深入讲存储？

note.zh: 主动管理时间，把选择权交给面试官。
note.en: Manage the clock and let them choose the next topic.

phrases.en: If we needed to handle ten times the traffic, the first thing I'd change is the cache layer.
phrases.zh: 如果流量变成十倍，我首先会改缓存层。

note.zh: 提前讲扩展方案，展示前瞻性。
note.en: Bringing up scaling early shows foresight.

dialogue.en: Let's design a URL shortener.
dialogue.zh: 我们来设计一个短链接服务。

dialogue.en: Sure. Before jumping into the design, I'd like to nail down the requirements. Do we need custom aliases, and should links expire?
dialogue.zh: 好的。开始设计前我想先把需求定下来。需要自定义别名吗？链接会过期吗？

dialogue.en: Custom aliases are a nice-to-have. No expiration for now.
dialogue.zh: 自定义别名可有可无，暂时不过期。

dialogue.en: Got it. I'd guess this is very read-heavy, maybe a hundred reads for every write. Let me do a quick back-of-the-envelope estimate of the storage.
dialogue.zh: 明白。我猜这是读远多于写，可能每写一次读一百次。我先粗略估算一下存储。

dialogue.en: Sounds good.
dialogue.zh: 好。

dialogue.en: Here's a high-level design: an API service, a key-value store for the mappings, and a cache in front of it for popular links. The main trade-off is how we generate the short codes.
dialogue.zh: 高层设计是：一个 API 服务、一个存映射的键值存储，以及前面放热门链接的缓存。主要的取舍在于短码怎么生成。

dialogue.en: What are the options?
dialogue.zh: 有哪些选择？

dialogue.en: We could hash the long URL, which is simple but can collide, or use a counter, which avoids collisions but needs coordination across servers. I'd lean toward a counter with pre-allocated ranges.
dialogue.zh: 可以对长链接做哈希，简单但可能冲突；或者用计数器，没有冲突但要跨服务器协调。我倾向于用预分配号段的计数器。

dialogue.en: Why?
dialogue.zh: 为什么？

dialogue.en: Because each server only talks to the coordinator when it runs out of IDs, so it's cheap. To keep an eye on the time, should I go deeper on that, or move on to caching?
dialogue.zh: 因为每台服务器只有在号段用完时才找协调者，开销很小。考虑到时间，我是深入讲这块，还是接着讲缓存？

cloze.en: Before jumping into the design, I'd like to ___ down the requirements.
cloze.zh: 在开始设计之前，我想先把需求定下来。

cloze.en: The main ___ here is consistency versus availability.
cloze.zh: 这里的主要取舍是一致性和可用性。

cloze.en: Given the write volume, I'd ___ toward a key-value store.
cloze.zh: 考虑到写入量，我更倾向于键值存储。

cloze.en: One ___ I see is the database during peak hours.
cloze.zh: 我看到的一个瓶颈是高峰期的数据库。

parts: and then we can dive into
order.zh: 先给一个高层设计，然后你想深入哪部分都可以。
缺点是失去强一致性，我认为对信息流来说可以接受。

blurb.zh: 准备两三个关于日常工作、成长和团队的问题，最后问清下一步流程。
blurb.en: Have two or three questions about the work, growth and the team ready, and finish by asking about next steps.

phrases.en: Yes, I have a few questions, if we have time.
phrases.zh: 有的，如果时间允许，我有几个问题。

note.zh: 别回答“没有问题”，至少准备两三个。
note.en: Never say you have no questions; have two or three ready.

phrases.en: What does a typical day look like for someone on this team?
phrases.zh: 这个团队的人一天通常是怎么过的？

note.zh: 了解日常工作的经典问题。
note.en: A classic way to learn about the day-to-day.

phrases.en: How do you measure success for this role in the first six months?
phrases.zh: 这个岗位前六个月怎么衡量做得好不好？

note.zh: 显示你关心结果，也能了解对方的期望。
note.en: Shows you care about results and reveals their expectations.

phrases.en: What's the biggest challenge the team is facing right now?
phrases.zh: 团队目前面临的最大挑战是什么？

note.zh: 回答往往能透露团队的真实状况。
note.en: The answer often tells you how things really are.

phrases.en: How does the team handle code reviews and on-call?
phrases.zh: 团队的代码评审和值班是怎么安排的？

note.zh: on-call（值班）是工程师很关心的话题。
note.en: On-call is something engineers rightly care about.

phrases.en: What do you enjoy most about working here?
phrases.zh: 你在这里工作最喜欢的是什么？

note.zh: 让面试官聊聊自己，气氛通常会轻松下来。
note.en: Getting them to talk about themselves lightens the mood.

phrases.en: How do new grads usually ramp up here?
phrases.zh: 应届生在这里通常怎么上手？

note.zh: ramp up 指上手、进入状态。
note.en: "Ramp up" means get up to speed.

phrases.en: Is there anything about my background that you'd like me to clarify?
phrases.zh: 关于我的背景，有什么需要我再说明的吗？

note.zh: 给自己一个消除顾虑的机会，语气要轻松。
note.en: Gives you a chance to address concerns; keep the tone relaxed.

phrases.en: What are the next steps in the process?
phrases.zh: 接下来的流程是什么？

note.zh: 最后一定要问，方便你安排时间。
note.en: Always ask, so you can plan your time.

phrases.en: Thanks, that's really helpful to know.
phrases.zh: 谢谢，这些信息很有帮助。

note.zh: 听完回答先回应一句，再问下一个。
note.en: Acknowledge the answer before your next question.

dialogue.en: We have about five minutes left. Do you have any questions for me?
dialogue.zh: 我们还剩大约五分钟，你有什么问题想问我吗？

dialogue.en: Yes, I have a few, thanks. What does a typical week look like for an engineer on your team?
dialogue.zh: 有几个，谢谢。你们团队的工程师一周通常是怎样的？

dialogue.en: Mostly feature work, with a planning meeting on Mondays and demos on Fridays.
dialogue.zh: 主要是做功能，周一有计划会，周五有演示。

dialogue.en: That sounds nice. How do you measure success for someone in this role during their first six months?
dialogue.zh: 听起来不错。这个岗位前六个月怎么衡量做得好不好？

dialogue.en: Shipping a project on your own by the end of the first quarter is a good sign.
dialogue.zh: 第一个季度结束时能独立上线一个项目，就是个好信号。

dialogue.en: That's really helpful to know. And what do you enjoy most about working here?
dialogue.zh: 这很有帮助。那你在这里工作最喜欢的是什么？

dialogue.en: Honestly, the people. Everyone's willing to help.
dialogue.zh: 说实话是这里的人，大家都乐于帮忙。

dialogue.en: Great. Last question: what are the next steps in the process?
dialogue.zh: 好的。最后一个问题：接下来的流程是什么？

cloze.en: What does a ___ day look like for someone on this team?
cloze.zh: 这个团队的人一天通常是怎么过的？

cloze.en: How do new grads usually ramp ___ here?
cloze.zh: 应届生在这里通常怎么上手？

cloze.en: What are the next ___ in the process?
cloze.zh: 接下来的流程是什么？

cloze.en: How do you ___ success for this role in the first six months?
cloze.zh: 这个岗位前六个月怎么衡量做得好不好？

order.zh: 团队目前面临的最大挑战是什么？
关于我的背景，有什么需要我再说明的吗？

blurb.zh: 接通时报名字、确认音质，信号不好时请对方重复，结束时具体地道谢。
blurb.en: Answer with your name, check the audio, ask for a repeat when the line drops, and close with a specific thank-you.

phrases.en: Hi, this is Wei speaking.
phrases.zh: 你好，我是 Wei。

note.zh: 接起面试电话时直接报名字，比只说 Hello? 更专业。
note.en: Answering with your name sounds more professional than "Hello?".

phrases.en: I'm doing well, thanks. How about you?
phrases.zh: 我挺好的，谢谢。你呢？

note.zh: 回答 How are you 之后要反问一句。
note.en: After "How are you?", ask it back.

phrases.en: Can you hear me okay?
phrases.zh: 你能听清我说话吗？

note.zh: 开始前确认一下音质，很常见。
note.en: Checking the audio at the start is common.

phrases.en: Sorry, you cut out for a second. Could you repeat the last part?
phrases.zh: 抱歉，刚才声音断了一下，能再说一遍最后那部分吗？

note.zh: cut out 指信号或声音断断续续。
note.en: "Cut out" means the audio dropped.

phrases.en: Sorry, could you say that one more time? I want to make sure I heard it right.
phrases.zh: 抱歉，能再说一次吗？我想确认我听对了。

note.zh: 没听清就直说，比猜错好。
note.en: Asking again beats guessing wrong.

phrases.en: Would you mind if I share my screen?
phrases.zh: 我可以共享屏幕吗？

note.zh: Would you mind if 的回答如果是 No，意思是“不介意”。
note.en: To "Would you mind if", a "No" means "go ahead".

phrases.en: I think we're about at time.
phrases.zh: 我想时间差不多到了。

note.zh: 留意时间，体面地把话题收住。
note.en: Watch the clock and wrap up gracefully.

phrases.en: Thanks so much for your time today. I really enjoyed our conversation.
phrases.zh: 非常感谢你今天抽出时间，我很喜欢这次交流。

note.zh: 提到聊过的某个具体话题，会显得更真诚。
note.en: Mention something specific you discussed to sound sincere.

phrases.en: I'm looking forward to hearing from you.
phrases.zh: 期待你的回复。

note.zh: 收尾的标准说法，邮件里也能用。
note.en: A standard closing that works in email too.

phrases.en: Have a great rest of your day.
phrases.zh: 祝你今天接下来一切顺利。

note.zh: 挂电话前的常用道别。
note.en: A common goodbye before hanging up.

dialogue.en: Hi, is this Wei?
dialogue.zh: 你好，是 Wei 吗？

dialogue.en: Yes, this is Wei speaking. Hi!
dialogue.zh: 是的，我是 Wei。你好！

dialogue.en: Hi Wei, this is Sam from the platform team. How are you doing today?
dialogue.zh: 你好 Wei，我是平台组的 Sam。今天过得怎么样？

dialogue.en: I'm doing well, thanks. How about you?
dialogue.zh: 挺好的，谢谢。你呢？

dialogue.en: Pretty good, thanks. Can you hear me okay?
dialogue.zh: 还不错，谢谢。你能听清我说话吗？

dialogue.en: Yes, loud and clear.
dialogue.zh: 能，很清楚。

dialogue.en: Okay, looks like we're about at time. Thanks for chatting with me.
dialogue.zh: 好，看起来时间差不多到了。谢谢你跟我聊。

dialogue.en: Thanks so much for your time today. I really enjoyed hearing about the migration project.
dialogue.zh: 非常感谢你今天抽出时间，我很喜欢听你讲那个迁移项目。

dialogue.en: Our recruiter will reach out within a week.
dialogue.zh: 我们的招聘人员会在一周内联系你。

dialogue.en: Sounds great. I'm looking forward to hearing from you. Have a great rest of your day!
dialogue.zh: 好的，期待你们的回复。祝你今天接下来一切顺利！

cloze.en: Sorry, you cut ___ for a second.
cloze.zh: 抱歉，刚才声音断了一下。

cloze.en: Can you hear me ___?
cloze.zh: 你能听清我说话吗？

cloze.en: I'm looking forward to ___ from you.
cloze.zh: 期待你的回复。

cloze.en: Thanks so much for your ___ today.
cloze.zh: 非常感谢你今天抽出时间。

order.zh: 我可以共享屏幕吗？
祝你今天接下来一切顺利。

title.zh: 和招聘方谈时间线与 offer

blurb.zh: 问清流程时间，说明手里的其他机会，拿到 offer 后要时间考虑，并有礼貌地谈数字。
blurb.en: Ask about the timeline, mention other processes, take time to review an offer, and negotiate the numbers politely.

phrases.en: Could you walk me through the timeline for the rest of the process?
phrases.zh: 能给我讲讲后面流程的时间安排吗？

note.zh: walk me through 意思是“一步步讲给我听”。
note.en: "Walk me through" asks for a step-by-step explanation.

phrases.en: I'm currently interviewing with a couple of other companies, so timing matters for me.
phrases.zh: 我目前也在面另外几家公司，所以时间对我比较重要。

note.zh: 如实说明，但不必透露公司名。
note.en: Be honest; you don't have to name the companies.

phrases.en: I have an offer with a deadline next Friday. Is there any way to speed things up?
phrases.zh: 我有一个下周五截止的 offer，有办法加快流程吗？

note.zh: 手里有带截止日期的 offer 时，尽早告诉招聘方。
note.en: Tell recruiters about a deadline as early as you can.

phrases.en: Thank you so much. I'm really excited about this offer.
phrases.zh: 非常感谢，我对这个 offer 很期待。

note.zh: 先表达感谢和兴趣，再谈细节。
note.en: Show thanks and interest before discussing details.

phrases.en: Could I have a few days to review the details?
phrases.zh: 我可以用几天时间看一下细节吗？

note.zh: 不必当场答应，要几天时间考虑很正常。
note.en: You don't have to accept on the spot; asking for a few days is normal.

phrases.en: Is there any flexibility on the base salary?
phrases.zh: 底薪有调整空间吗？

note.zh: flexibility 是开启谈薪的委婉用词。
note.en: "Flexibility" is a soft way to open a negotiation.

phrases.en: Based on my research and other offers, I was hoping for something closer to one-forty.
phrases.zh: 根据我的调研和其他 offer，我希望能接近 14 万。

note.zh: 14 万美元口语常说 one-forty；先给依据，再报数字。
note.en: People say "one-forty" for 140,000; give your basis, then the number.

phrases.en: Could you share how the equity vests?
phrases.zh: 能说一下股票是怎么归属的吗？

note.zh: vest 指股票按时间表归属，问清归属节奏。
note.en: To vest is to earn equity over time; ask for the schedule.

phrases.en: If we can get there on the sign-on bonus, I'm ready to sign.
phrases.zh: 如果签字费能做到这个数，我就可以签了。

note.zh: 明确的条件句能让谈判更快收尾。
note.en: A clear "if ... then" helps close the deal.

phrases.en: I appreciate you working with me on this.
phrases.zh: 感谢你在这件事上帮我争取。

note.zh: 谈判之后感谢招聘方，关系会更好。
note.en: Thanking the recruiter keeps the relationship good.

dialogue.en: Hi! I have some great news: the team would like to make you an offer.
dialogue.zh: 你好！好消息：团队想给你发 offer。

dialogue.en: That's wonderful, thank you so much! I'm really excited about this.
dialogue.zh: 太好了，非常感谢！我对此很期待。

dialogue.en: The base is a hundred and twenty-five thousand, plus equity and a sign-on bonus. I'll email you the details.
dialogue.zh: 底薪 12.5 万，另有股票和签字费。我会把细节发邮件给你。

dialogue.en: Thank you. Could I have a few days to review everything?
dialogue.zh: 谢谢。我可以用几天时间看一下吗？

dialogue.en: Of course. Is there anything on your mind already?
dialogue.zh: 当然。你现在有什么想法吗？

dialogue.en: To be transparent, I have another offer with a deadline next Friday. Based on that and my research, I was hoping for a base closer to one-forty. Is there any flexibility there?
dialogue.zh: 坦白说，我有另一个下周五截止的 offer。基于那个 offer 和我的调研，我希望底薪能接近 14 万。这方面有调整空间吗？

dialogue.en: I can't promise anything, but I'll talk to the team.
dialogue.zh: 我不能保证，但我会和团队沟通。

dialogue.en: I appreciate you working with me on this. If we can get closer to that number, I'd be ready to sign.
dialogue.zh: 感谢你帮我争取。如果能更接近这个数字，我就可以签。

cloze.en: Could you walk me ___ the timeline?
cloze.zh: 能给我讲讲时间安排吗？

cloze.en: Is there any ___ on the base salary?
cloze.zh: 底薪有调整空间吗？

cloze.en: Could you share how the equity ___?
cloze.zh: 能说一下股票是怎么归属的吗？

cloze.en: Could I have a few days to ___ the details?
cloze.zh: 我可以用几天时间看一下细节吗？

order.zh: 我有一个下周五截止的 offer，有办法加快流程吗？
感谢你在这件事上帮我争取。
